acceptanceCriteria: A rubric file with stable rule IDs exists and its authority is recorded in a decision.
Codex review lane prompts and the reviewer report cite rule IDs in findings.
Each MUST rule names its enforcing check or test, or is marked unenforced.
body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix keeps a checked-in REVIEW.md using RFC 2119 keywords in sections Always check, Patterns to flag, Security and Skip, with concrete test-backed rules (e.g. a privileged operation needs a regression test asserting its location and required permission). Corvint has no repository rubric; Codex review prompts are hand-written per lane, so review criteria drift between lanes. Proposal: a project-owned rubric that the CEM reviewer report and Codex review prompts both cite, so review findings trace to a stable rule ID (invariant 3: project authority outranks syntax and learned traces). Candidate rules from this session: bounded reads, NOT_RUN never reported as passed, test temp paths under the 128-byte gate argv limit, no unbounded os.Getwd inheritance, error-code ownership.
title: Project-owned reviewer rubric (REVIEW.md) consumed by the reviewer report and Codex review lanes
